 :Judgment:
This claim petition emanates in respect of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner by name Sri Muruli B in respect of the Road Traffic Accident dated 02.08.2023.

2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
That on 02.08.2023 at about 5.40 to 5.50 p.m., when the petitioner was proceeding in a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 04-HQ-8677 as a pillion rider along with rider by name SCCH 15 3 MVC No.7091/2023 Thippeswamy and when they reached near Bettahalli cross, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru, at that time, respondent's motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EN-4622 (herein after referred to as the offending vehicle)
came from Lakshmipura side in a rash and negligent manner with excessive speed, in order to overtake a vehicle and dashed against the Petitioner's motorcycle, resulting in the accident.
It is submitted that the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
3. Immediately, after the accident petitioner was shifted to Arkavathi hospital, after first aid treatment, he was shifted to Hosmat hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
Hence, the petitioner has claimed compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
4. In pursuance of service of notice issued to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
SCCH 15 4 MVC No.7091/2023

The Respondent No.2 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
The respondent No.2 admitted that it has issued insurance policy to the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EN-4622 in favour of the respondent No.1.
Without prejudice the liability of the respondent No.2 if any is subject to the validity of driving license and terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
The rider of the said vehicle did not have valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.
It is submitted that the amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant, excessive, arbitrary, unreasonable and without any legal basis.
Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

Vide order dated 06.11.2024 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road SCCH 15 5 MVC No.7091/2023 Traffic Accident that occurred on 02.08.2023 at about 5.40 p.m., near Bettahalli cross, Dasanapura hobli, Bengaluru district, due to t h e r a s h a n d n e g l i g e n t r i d i n g o f t h e r i d e r o f m o t o r c y c l e b e a r i n g Reg.No.KA-51-EN-4622?

2) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for? If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?
3) What Order or Award?
6. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to 27 documents.

The Learned Counsel for the respondent No.2 has relied on the following citations:
1. MFA No.1800/2013 (MV), between Raghunatha Murthy Vs. Samuel & another 2. MFA No.3430/2014, between Arun Karadi Vs. The Regional Manager & another SCCH 15 6 MVC No.7091/2023 7.

entities.text: Arun Karadi Vs. The Regional Manager & another SCCH 15 6 MVC No.7091/2023 7

sentences.text: Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order
for the following :
REASONS 8. Issue No.1: Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.
It is the contention of the petitioner that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EN- 4622 / offending vehicle.

9. In this regard the petitioner has got examined himself as PW.1 and in his chief-examination he has deposed that on 02.08.2023 at about 5.40 to 5.50 p.m., when the petitioner was proceeding in motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HQ-8677 as a pillion rider along with rider by name Thippeswamy, SCCH 15 7 MVC No.7091/2023 proceeding from Kadabagere - Madanayakanahalli Muruli B vs Hareesh Kumar V on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136653395/
3 road and when they reached near Bettahalli cross slowly and cautiously, the rider of the offending came in a rash and negligent manner with excessive speed, without observing traffic rules and in order to overtake another vehicle, dashed against the Petitioner's motorcycle, resulting in the accident.
Consequently, petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
10. The petitioner in support of his claim has in addition to describing the course of the accident in line with the facts mentioned in the complaint has relied upon Ex.P1 to 8 documents.

Ex.P1 is the FIR which is registered against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offenses under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC and Sec.187 of MV Act on the basis of the complaint given by wife of the petitioner on 03.08.2023.
As far as the delay in lodging the complaint, it is submitted by the petitioner he was undergoing treatment in the hospital, hence, there is a delay in lodging the complaint.

Further Ex.P3 is the spot mahazar which discloses the spot of the accident and SCCH 15 8 MVC No.7091/2023 spot of the accident is towards left side of the road from Bettahalli cross, little ahead of the bridge from north towards south.
The documents discloses that the offending vehicle rider in order to overtake a lorry, came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the petitioner's motorcycle.
Ex.P6 is the wound certificate which discloses that the petitioner had sustained injuries due to the impact of the accident.
Ex.P7 is the IMV report which discloses the damages caused to the vehicle.

Ex.P8 is the charge sheet filed after completion of investigation against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offences under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC and Sec.187 of MV Act and contents of the charge sheet discloses that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.

11. As far as the manner of the accident is concerned PW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 and in the cross-examination of PW.1, he has deposed that he was going along with Tippeswamy and he was SCCH 15 9 MVC No.7091/2023 going for plumbing work and the motorcycle came from ahead and dashed their bike.
He has deposed that the accident spot is curve road and denied that the accident occurred since he was talking with his friend and did not notice oncoming motorcycle.

Except the suggestion that the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the petitioner's side nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence or rashness on the part of petitioner by leading rebuttal evidence.
The petitioner has clearly and categorically deposed about the manner of the accident.
The oral testimony of PW.1 has stood unrebutted and PW1 has withstood the cross-examination of Respondent No.2.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
PW.1 has also denied the suggestion imputing the cause of the accident to be due to his negligence.

The fact that the rider of the offending vehicle has already been charge SCCH 15 10 MVC No.7091/2023 sheeted for the offenses under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC and Sec.187 of MV Act itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.

The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet,
IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 in the above accident.
In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that PW.1 suffered grievous injuries on account of rashness and negligence of rider riding the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

Hence,
issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioner and in the 'Affirmative'.

sentences.text: 4 12. Issue No.2
: In view of the findings on issue No.1 in favour of petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
The computation of compensation will have to be decided separately under various heads.
13. MEDICAL OR TREATMENT EXPENSES:

The petitioner has produced Ex.P6 wound certificate which discloses that the petitioner has sustained fracture mid shaft SCCH 15 11 MVC No.7091/2023 of RT radius and fracture right 3 rd, 4th and 5th metatarsal bone with degloving injury.
The said document discloses that he has taken treatment with respect to the injuries sustained in the accident.
In addition the petitioner has produced Ex.P10 to 17 are Discharge summaries, medical bills, Photos and X-rays.

As far as the medical bills are concerned PW.1 is cross- examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 and in the cross-examination PW.1 has admitted that some of the medical bills have been reimbursed.
Except this nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination to doubt authenticity of the bills produced by the petitioner and to prove reimbursement.
Hence in view of the medical bills produced and taking them into consideration the petitioner is awarded an amount of Rs.86,814/- under this head.
14. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

As per the medical documents the petitioner has suffered fracture mid shaft of RT radius and fracture right 3rd, 4th and 5th metatarsal bone with degloving injury and it is stated in the petition that injuries SCCH 15 12 MVC No.7091/2023 sustained and physical impairment has caused unbearable pain and petitioner cannot do any work as prior to the accident and unable to walk normally, sit down, squat and sit cross leg, lift weights in the right hand.
It is not possible to ascertain quantum of compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc., which he actually suffered due to the accidental injuries.

Keeping in view the trauma and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc.,
an amount of Rs.30,000/- is awarded to him towards pain and sufferings.
Thus, he is awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
15. LOSS OF ACTUAL EARNINGS:
As far as the income is concerned PW.1 has deposed that he was Police officer and having salary of Rs.40,000/- p.m.,
In his cross-examination he has admitted that he is working as a driver of Reserve Police as AHCOOD and having monthly Rs.60,000/- and at the time of accident salary was Rs.44,000/- p.m.,
In the support of the SCCH 15 13 MVC No.7091/2023 same, petitioner has produced Ex.P18 - ID card.
The fact that the petitioner is continuing with the same job goes to show that the petitioner has not suffered any loss of income due to laid up period.
In addition no evidence is adduced to show that his leave was without pay.
Hence, the petitioner is not awarded any compensation amount under this head.
16. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS DUE TO DISABILITY:
The Petitioner has stated that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is not able to do his work as earlier.
17. In support of the same, PW.3 - Orthopedic Surgeon is examined and got marked clinical note and X-ray at Ex.P26 and 27.
PW.1 has deposed in his cross-examination that at present he is receiving salary of Rs.60,000/- per month.
Hence, it is crystal clear that he is continuing in his job.

sentences.text: In addition PW1 has also admitted that he is continuing his job and his salary is also enhanced as prior to the date of the SCCH 15 14 MVC No.7091/2023 accident.
There is no evidence to show that he has suffered loss of any increment or promotion due to the disablement.
Hence, he is not awarded any compensation under this head since he has not suffered any functional disability due to the injuries sustained in the accident and has no loss of future income.
18. Loss of Amenities:

In view of the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the extent of permanent physical disability and the extended period of medical treatment, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
19. Attendant's charges, Special diet and Conveyance:
The facts show that physical condition of the petitioner is such that he might have to taken the help of an attendant.
Further, he would be requiring conveyance for movement.
His avocation has been hit due to his injuries.
He might have spent considerable amount towards special diet during his treatment.
Therefore, petitioner is granted Rs.20,000/- under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE  PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  30,000/-
2. Loss of amenities  20,000/-
3. Loss of income during the laid ---- up period 4. Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  20,000/-
and conveyance 5.

Medical expenses  86,814/-
6. Loss of Future Income ---- Muruli B vs Hareesh Kumar V on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136653395/
6 Total  1,56,814/-
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 1,56,814/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

21. Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS.
SCCH 15 16 MVC No.7091/2023 RAJASTAN VS. SMT. LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.

sentences.text: Hence the rate of interest is set at 6% per annum in this case.

22. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EN-4622.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1 and has to pay compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.1 and 2 U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 1,56,814/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

Since, the amount awarded to the Petitioner is meager, the entire amount awarded to Petitioner shall be released to SCCH 15 18 MVC No.7091/2023 him by way of E- payment after his proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
